recheckedOn.scope: Only what can be re-checked mechanically, plus the targeted passes recorded under the named keys below: the scenario and terrain GUIDs, the startup parameters the documents call absent, the pre-0.9.8.73 field names, where player data and bans are stored, the RCON transport and packet format, the length limits the config schema applies to game.name, and the backend API surface with ownerToken.bin - including a captured dedicated-server registration. Everything else in docs/ remains a statement about the pinned build.

result.rconTransport: UDP — verified by running a non-public server on 1.8.0.13 (bound to 127.0.0.1, visible false) with rcon.address and rcon.port set: the RCON port was a UDP endpoint owned by the server process, there was no TCP listener on it, and a TCP connect was refused. Controls: the game port and the A2S port were UDP as well, which is what makes the negative result meaningful. The server's own line `[RCON] Init, Ip address=..., Port=...` carries no protocol information, which is why this stayed open. The packet format remains undocumented.

schemaAcceptanceSettledByLaunchingTheSer.note: dedicatedServerId and region were documented as 'not in the server config schema'. Running 1.8.0.13 with either key set reaches `JSON is Valid`, so they are undocumented fields rather than obsolete names. playerCountLimit and supportedGameClientTypes, though present as strings in that executable, are rejected by the schema.

rconProtocol.where: docs/en/ArmaReforger_RCON_EN.md §1.1, the RU mirror in docs/ru/
rconProtocol.result: The RCON packets are BattlEye RCon Protocol v2: a 7-byte header 'B' 0x42 | 'E' 0x45 | CRC32 of the following bytes, little-endian | 0xFF, then 0x00|password (login), 0x00|0x01 or 0x00|0x00 (login answer), 0x01|seq|command, 0x01|seq[|response] (command accepted), 0x02|seq|text (console message, must be answered with 0x02|seq) and 0x01|seq (empty keep-alive).
rconProtocol.crc: crc32(0xFF|payload), little-endian — checked against the server's own replies: for the login answer `BE 69 DD DE 36 FF 00 01` the stored value is 0x36DEDD69 and crc32(FF 00 01) = 0x36DEDD69.
rconProtocol.crcNotEnforced: Four logins in a row were authorized with the checksum computed over the payload alone and over 0xFF|payload, each little-endian and big-endian, so the CRC of incoming packets is not checked. A login sent as a bare payload without the 7-byte header got no answer at all.
rconProtocol.sequenceNumber: The command's seq is checked and a mismatch is silent: the same `players` sent as 01 00 was acknowledged and executed (`Received Game Command: players`), while as 01 07 it was acknowledged with 01 07 and otherwise ignored — no game command, no message, and no `Mismatched sequence number!` line, although that string is in the binary. The counter did not move either: the next packet from that session, `01 00 | @logout`, was still accepted.
rconProtocol.logout: `@logout` is a protocol command sent as 0x01|seq|@logout (seq 0 as the first command of a session) and it frees the slot at once: the server logs `[RCON] [CLIENT: 0] Received Protocol Command: @logout` and `[RCON] Client 0 logged out!`, the next login is counted as [1/4] rather than [2/4], and with rcon.maxClients 1 three consecutive players runs, a five-framing probe and a shell session were each authorized as #0 at [1/1] with no `Client List is full!` line anywhere. The BattlEye v2 specification defines no logout packet, so this is Bohemia's own addition; the wiki's 'RCON only, since 1.2.1' holds on 1.8.0.13. It is available under rcon.permission monitor as well as admin: on a monitor server that refused `kick 1` and `ban list 1` with `missing permission '<command>'`, three consecutive players runs on maxClients 1 were still each authorized as #0 at [1/1] with the logout freeing the slot between them, and probe (four framings authorized) and shell behaved the same way.
rconProtocol.engineAnswers: A command that does not run is answered with one of four engine texts, all of them *after* `Processing Command: <command>`, so a 0x01|seq acknowledgement plus a Processing note still does not mean the command ran: `missing permission '<command>'` (above rcon.permission — kick 1 and ban list 1 on a monitor server), `unknown command '<text>'`, `invalid parameters '<command>'` (too few arguments — kick, ban create, ban create 1), and `the server is busy` (a BUSY result). The binary carries the four literals in one table next to `RCONCommandHandler: Executing command {%s}.` and composes them with the format `%s '%s'`; that is also the English text behind the #AR-ServerCommands_PermissionError / _UnknownCommand / _ParametersError keys. The first three were observed live on 1.8.0.13, `the server is busy` was not reproduced. A bare `ban` is not among them: the server answers with its help screen, and `ban foo`/`ban help` get the same one — but the client's own grammar (the `usageError` check, shared by the command line and the shell) refuses `ban`, `ban create 1`, `ban remove`, `ban foo` and `kick` before a packet is sent, as usage errors (exit 2), so the help screen is only ever seen through the raw `cmd ban` path, where it is classified as a missing-parameter failure (exit 5). `kick 1 2` ignores the extra argument and answers `Player not found`. An unknown protocol command such as `@foo` is acknowledged with 0x01|seq and answered with no message at all, which is why the client decides that no answer (exit 4) came back by looking at the messages and not at the packets. `#restart` is the one game command observed answering nothing at all after its Processing note, which is why silence alone is not a failure.
rconProtocol.timeoutAndKeepAlive: The 45-second rule is real and was measured: four clients authorized at 01:25:40-01:25:51 were dropped 45-48 s later in authorization order, so a client that is merely closed keeps its maxClients slot for that long. The specification's empty keep-alive (0x01|seq, an empty 2-byte command packet) holds the session instead: a session left idle for 80 s with one every 20 s still answered `players`.
rconProtocol.howItWasDone: A dedicated server 1.8.0.13, non-public, rcon.address 127.0.0.1, rcon.port 19999, permission admin, and a client written for the experiment (kept out of the repository, in the gitignored out/). The logout, sequence, timeout and keep-alive findings come from the same build on rcon.maxClients 4 and then 1, with the server's own [RCON] lines read against the client count of each following login; the monitor run used the same config with permission monitor and maxClients 1, and the argument-less commands (kick, ban, ban create, kick 1 2, restart) were run with permission admin.
rconProtocol.stillOpen: Whether a BattlEye RCON client interoperates with rcon.port (not tried), and whether the missing CRC check is deliberate.

gameNameBounds.where: docs/en/ArmaReforger_ServerConfig_EN.md §5.4 and §9, the RU mirror in docs/ru/, schemas/server.schema.json, tests/fixtures/name-empty.invalid.json and name-too-long.invalid.json
gameNameBounds.result: The config schema bounds game.name at both ends and a violation is a rejection, not a crop. An empty string gives 'Param "#/game/name" is bellow the minimum limit of value/length. The minimum allowed is 1.'; 101 characters give 'Param "#/game/name" has surpassed the maximum limit of value/length. The maximum allowed is 100.'. Both are followed by 'Reference in schema: "#/properties/game/properties/name"', 'JSON is invalid!', 'There are errors in server config!' and the server ending by itself. Names of 1, 2, 3 and 100 characters all reached 'JSON is Valid' and the session started.
gameNameBounds.whyItMatters: The guide said 'string 0..100' and described a too long name as cropped by 'Session name exceed max value > N, cropped under limit...'. That string is in the executable, but it is not reached from server.json — the schema stops the server first. The lower bound is 1 character, not the 3-4 sometimes assumed for a server name.
gameNameBounds.control: The same build rejects a 2-character rcon.password with '... is bellow the minimum limit of value/length. The minimum allowed is 3.', so the validator does apply minLength when the schema declares one. The accepted 1-character name is therefore evidence about the schema, not about a missing check.
gameNameBounds.howItWasDone: A dedicated server 1.8.0.13 launched with tools/probe-config-schema.mjs, one config per name length (0, 1, 2, 3, 100, 101 characters), a fresh profile for each.

backendApiAndOwnerToken.where: docs/en/ArmaReforger_BackendAPI_EN.md, the RU mirror in docs/ru/, and docs/en/ArmaReforger_Profile_EN.md section 3 (RU mirror too)
backendApiAndOwnerToken.ownerTokenIsAJwt: ownerToken.bin is plain ASCII: a JWT, header {"alg":"RS512"}, unencrypted payload {iat, serverId, serverType, ownerType} plus ownerId when ownerType is GameIdentity. Five files were decoded - the game client's profile, Documents\My Games\ArmaReforgerServer\profile, Documents\My Games\test\profile, the dedicated server's own test\profile and the probe profile under out\ban-probe. ownerType is Anonymous in the four server profiles and GameIdentity in the client's; serverId differs in all five; serverType is CommunitySelfHosted in all five; and in all five the file's creation time equals the iat claim to the second (deltas 0, +2, +1, +1, +2 s), so the token is written when it is minted and never refreshed in place.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.whoIssuesIt: The backend, in the answer to the server's own registration call. Captured on the wire through a TLS-terminating proxy: POST https://api-ar-game.bistudio.com/game-api/s2s-api/v1.0/lobby/dedicatedServers/registerUnmanagedServer answers 200 with {"dsConfig":{...},"ownerToken":"..."}; the server writes that member to $profile:ownerToken.bin (file created 05:11:48, iat 1792116708) and replays the same JWT as accessToken on the following POST .../lobby/rooms/register. The token's serverId equals that answer's dsConfig.providerServerId, which is also the roomId. The binary carries dedicatedServers/registerUnmanagedServer (DSUnmanagedRegisterS2S) and the field ownerToken beside dsConfig. dedicatedServers/createOwnerToken exists in the same binary but was called in no captured dedicated-server run, so it is not the dedicated server's route - the client's token (ownerType GameIdentity with an ownerId) is the likely product of that other route, which was not captured.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.capturedOnTheWire: Before registration, five calls: GET https://api-ar-gc.bistudio.com/game-config/api/v1/reforger/1.8.0/13/list (200), GET https://api-ar-game.bistudio.com/game-api/api/v1.0/world?platformId=ReforgerSteam&clientVersion=1.8.0 (200), GET https://reforger.armaplatform.com/api/popup?loc=en_us (200), POST .../game-api/s2s-api/v1.0/lobby/dedicatedServers/registerUnmanagedServer (200, carries ownerToken), POST .../game-api/s2s-api/v1.0/lobby/rooms/register (200, roomId + mpRoom with directJoinCode and pingSiteId). While running, from the second pass: POST .../lobby/dedicatedServers/heartBeat 61 s after registration and 61 s later (200; the body carries id, state HostingGame, players[] and a stats block of @type aggregation/single), POST .../lobby/rooms/createBan ({"userId","reason","banDuration"}) -> {status:OK}, POST .../lobby/rooms/listActiveBans ({"page":{"limit":25}}) -> the ban record {id,targetType:'gid',targetId,targetName,currentName,scope:'reforger:<roomId>:join',type:'gameServer',reason,issuer:'room <roomId>',createdAt,expiresAt}, POST .../lobby/rooms/removeBans ({"userIds":[...]}) -> {status:OK}, and on RCON shutdown POST .../lobby/rooms/remove -> {status:OK}. Every S2S call carries the owner token as accessToken plus dedicatedServerId and roomId. A configured mod goes through POST https://api-ar-workshop.bistudio.com/workshop-api/api/v3.0/s2s/assets/download-list (200; version, gameVersion and the files with their manifestPath) and then GET https://ar-gcp-cdn.bistudio.com/manifest/... and /fragment/... until 'Required addons are ready to use.' The registration POSTs are chunked with Expect: 100-continue and carry x-client-id ($edb1b7862bba5cade1f6e06bfdeac2c), x-client-secret (32 chars) and user-agent 'Arma Reforger/1.8.0.13 (Headless; Windows)'; the answers come from Cloudflare with x-signature-validation-result: true. The registration body carries playerCountLimit and supportedGameClientTypes, which server.json rejects, and the room body carries game.password in clear. Nothing under servers/*, server-configs/*, dedicatedServers/createOwnerToken, storage, groups or notifications was called, and nobody joined the server.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.incompatibleModTakesTheServerDown: The mod the second pass fetched (6653028F468BD115, GTG_Licences, built for game version 1.4.0.55) downloaded without complaint - the download list does not filter by compatibility - and then failed to compile against 1.8.0.13: crash.log says 'Can't compile "Game" script module! scripts/Game/Player/Modded/SCR_PlayerController.c(1): Expected attribute call', the console says 'Unable to initialize the game' and 'Game destroyed.', and the Windows crash reporter window appeared. The user dismissed it, so nothing was sent to Bohemia.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.playerFacingCallsAndTheCareerWrite: A real player joined a probe server from the same machine (three attempts: the first client launch failed to initialise with the mods in his own profile, the second and third joined). Captured: GET /game-api/api/v1.0/dummy right before the join and before the leave (200, body {}, no credential of any kind); POST .../lobby/rooms/acceptPlayer with sessionTicket (512 chars) answering userProfile (currencies, countryCode, overallPlayTime, tester, isDeveloperAccount), platformIdentities {biAccountId, steamId} and character.data, a JSON string holding the whole 39-value m_aStats; POST .../lobby/rooms/removePlayer with userId, expireIn 4995 and removeEvent {group:1, reason:9}, answering {status:OK, expireAt}; and the heartbeat then carrying players:[{identity:<uuid>}]. The identityId that joined equals the ownerId inside the client's own ownerToken.bin, which closes the loop on that file. The career WRITE never appeared - not on a 120 s timer during seven minutes of play, not on the player leaving, not on a clean shutdown and not on RCON #restart (four scenarios). The reason is in the code: SCR_PlayerProfileManagerComponent.OnPlayerDisconnected calls StoreProfile(playerId, true) which ends in PlayerCharacterUpdateS2S, but LoadPlayerProfileFromBackend() creates the profile object it needs only while GetBackendApi().GetDSSession().Status() == EDSESSION_ACTIVE, and StoreProfile returns on its first line without it; a community server never opens that session, so the career travels one way only, in the acceptPlayer answer.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.platformIdentityResolution: Asked whether an identityId can be resolved to a platform, a store and an account: while the player is in the session the server already has it, from the acceptPlayer answer (gameClientType, currentDeviceType, platformUsername, platformIdentities.steamId in full) and from the script accessors BackendApi.GetPlayerPlatformKind/GetPlayerPlatformId, whose enum is PlatformKind { NONE, XBOX, PSN, STEAM } (scripts/GameLib/generated/PlatformKind.c). Both accessors are marked [Obsolete] in arexplorer 1.7.0.54 and both names are in the 1.8.0.13 binary, which still calls them (the server's own log warns at SCR_EditableEntityComponent.c,785-786). By identity alone nothing was observed: RCON #players prints playerId|uid|name, the ban record carries targetId/targetName/currentName, and the candidates in the binary (GameApiListGetUserMetadata on userProfiles/getMetadata with a users array, the fields platformIds and targetId, the GameApiV2 user/gameData/* family keyed by userIds) were never called. The console ids are hashed (xboxIdHash, psnIdHash) while only steamId is raw, which is an inference from field names because no console player was captured, and there is no profile URL template anywhere in the server binary - only ShowUserProfile on the client. Also recorded: biAccountId arrives in the acceptPlayer JSON but the string appears in neither the server nor the client binary, so no class declares it and it is dropped on expansion like the blacklist/whitelist/admins arrays.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.userProfilesGetMetadataProbe: The one endpoint that looks like it resolves an identityId to a platform was asked directly, outside the game, with the API's own client headers captured from a probe server. POST https://api-ar-game.bistudio.com/game-api/api/v1.0/userProfiles/getMetadata exists (GET answers 404 'There is no Msg handler for GET ...'), and its handler's own validation gave the request shape: a body with `users` answers "Field 'userIds' must not be null, found: null." (so the field is userIds), and once userIds is present it answers "accessToken can't be empty". The accessToken it wants is a user token: the dedicated server's owner token is rejected with 'Unsupported accessToken type', and so is the game client's own owner token, whose payload carries ownerType GameIdentity. So a dedicated server cannot resolve an identity to a platform this way. The answer is unobserved, but the response class is GameApiListGetUserMetadataResponse and its RTTI names UserMetadata with a nested Platform struct, so platform data is what the call is for. Whether it is scoped to the token's own identity was not tested, deliberately. The refusals also documented the API's error envelope, {code, apiCode, message, uid}, whose message names the offending fields - which is how the request shape was established.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.serverTokenOAuthFlow: The GameApiV2 server-token family was opened from outside the game with nothing but the client credentials the build ships. POST /game-api/api/v2.0/servers/createToken answers 200 with a fresh anonymous server token ({"serverToken","persistent":false,"serverType":2,"serverId"}; a new serverId every call, serverType 2 = CommunitySelfHosted, an RS512 JWS of 534 characters), which also settles the prefix: this family is /game-api/api/v2.0/, while /game-api/s2s-api/v2.0/ answers 404 with no handler. POST /api/v2.0/servers/auth with `Authorization: ServerToken <that token>` answers 200 with {"serverAccessToken","serverType","serverId","expireIn":1800}: an RS256 JWS with a kid, TTL 30 minutes, payload {iat, exp, id, aid, t} where id is the serverId and exp = iat + expireIn. The auth type took two batches to find - a request without a type is answered with the expected format ('Invalid Authorization header. Expected format 'Authorization: <type> <value>'.') and a wrong word with 'Invalid auth type <word>'; Bearer, Basic, Token, JWT, Client, Steam, Server, Owner, S2S, Anonymous, None, ApiKey, ClientSecret, serverToken, ownerToken, gameClientToken, identityToken, accessToken and CommunitySelfHosted are all refused. /servers/auth/refresh wants the same header type and the server token again, not the access token ('InvalidServerToken: Invalid JWT token'; no header at all gives 'AuthError: Missing server auth.'). What the access token unlocks was not mapped beyond one negative result: userProfiles/getMetadata refuses it with 'Unsupported accessToken type', like the owner tokens, so it is a server-typed token and does not open the user-facing call.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.whereTheBaseUrlsComeFrom: The API's base URLs are delivered by the backend, not hardcoded: the game config answer's properties array (42 entries) carries them under the binary's own URI_* context names - URI_GameApi https://api-ar-game.bistudio.com/game-api/api/v1.0/, URI_GameApiS2S .../s2s-api/v1.0/, URI_LobbyApi .../s2s-api/v1.0/lobby/, URI_ClientLobbyApi .../api/v1.0/lobby/, URI_IdentityApi https://api-ar-id.bistudio.com/game-identity/, URI_UserApi https://api.bistudio.com/user/api/v2.0/, URI_AccountApi https://accounts.bistudio.com/auth, URI_StorageApi https://api-ar-storage.bistudio.com/storage/api/v4.0/, URI_WorkshopApi https://api-ar-workshop.bistudio.com/workshop-api/api/v3.0/, URI_ContentApi https://ar-gcp-cdn.bistudio.com/, URI_GroupApi https://api-ar-group.bistudio.com/group/api/v2.0/, URI_NewsApi/URI_NotifyApi/URI_PopUpApi on reforger.armaplatform.com, URI_STSApi https://br4cju2z.ts.steelshield.me/v1/bohemia/armareforger/, URI_STSContext .../game-identity/api/v1.1/nitrado/steel-shield/reforger/, URI_AnalyticsApi and URI_TreasureData on in.treasuredata.com, and URI_StarRiver with no value at all. The remaining entries are the Link_* menu addresses and two option blobs. This is why no address is a literal in the executable and why the map can change without a client patch; the captured config names no URI_GameApiV2 even though /game-api/api/v2.0/servers/auth answers, so that base is either derived from URI_GameApi or carried by a different config. Whether these are production addresses in general or only what this build in this region was handed was not established.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.clientEndpointsNeedAUserToken: Asked whether the player list leads anywhere: it does not, from a server. The profile action is client-side and platform-delegated - PlayerManager.ShowUserProfile(playerId), documented as 'Shows platform specific UI with the profile of specified player', with PlayerManager.IsUserProfileAvailable(playerId) deciding whether the button appears and SCR_PlayerListMenu.UpdateViewProfileButton(playerId) (and the group-list twin, and the blocked-users dialog) hiding or showing it - so the profile is opened by the platform's own overlay from the player's platform account, not by asking the backend for a URL. The client-side call that would list a room's players, POST /game-api/api/v1.0/lobby/rooms/listPlayers (on URI_ClientLobbyApi), exists - it was probed against a live registered room - but refuses every server-typed credential with 'Unsupported accessToken type': the owner token from registration, the game client's own owner token (ownerType GameIdentity) and a freshly minted serverAccessToken. The token it wants comes from the account flow: POST https://api.bistudio.com/user/api/v2.0/auth/login answers '<body> should have required property client_id' with the user API's own error shape, and the identity service is a Spring application answering {timestamp,status,error,path}. So every client-facing endpoint needs a real logged-in user's access token, and what those calls answer remains unseen.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.userLoginFlow: The client's login was mapped from outside by probing, with no user credentials: POST https://api.bistudio.com/user/api/v2.0/auth/login (the executable's UserApiDirectAuth) requires exactly one body field, client_id, and it must match ^\$[A-Za-z0-9]{31}$ - the same $+31 id the build sends as the x-client-id header, so the call authenticates the application by the credential it already carries; a wrong-but-well-shaped id is not distinguished from the right one. With a well-formed body and no session the answer is 401 {'code':401,'message':'Unauthorized','uid':<number>,'desc':'UNAUTHORIZED'} - no apiCode, no api_code. The binary's field list for the call is client_id, two_factor_token, access_token. Its sibling game-identity/token answers 401 rather than 404 under the same base (https://api.bistudio.com/user/api/v2.0/game-identity/token), which is why the game config's URI_IdentityApi plus that string is a 404: that is where a client's GameIdentity token comes from. Step one of the flow is the browser at accounts.bistudio.com/auth, the config's URI_AccountApi - no such string is in the client binary either, because the client reads the same config. The class list in the executable (UserApiDirectAuth with Request/Response/ErrorResponseDirectAuth, UserApiGetUser, IdentityApiAuth/Create/Link/Unlink and their request/response types, WorkshopApiDelegationTokens, GameApiSessionLogin) and the error vocabulary it maps (authService.invalidCredentials, authService.missing2FA, authService.invalid2FA, userService.userLocked, userService.notFound, accountLocked, UnauthorizedToken, UnknownIdentity, ConflictIdentity, SteamConnectionError, servers.notFound.canRegister/doNotContinue) say the second factor is handled in that call and that linking a platform account is where SteamConnectionError comes from. Also settled: auth/delegationTokens is a Workshop API path, not a user one - POST /workshop-api/api/v3.0/auth/delegationTokens answers 401 {'message','apiCode':'Unauthorized','errors':[],'meta':{},'uid':'<ts>-<n>'}, a fourth error shape. The successful answer of auth/login was never seen (class UserApiResponseDirectAuth, no field observed), and a dedicated server cannot walk the flow at all, which is why client-facing calls answer Unsupported accessToken type to every server credential.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.apiSurface: The endpoint, operation and field names in the backend document are strings and RTTI symbols of ArmaReforgerServer.exe 1.8.0.13 (blocks around 0x1A8xxxx-0x1A9xxxx for paths, 0x1A47Dxx-0x1A47Fxx for the CLI/config keys, 0x205xxxx-0x207xxxx for class names), including the URI_* context names and the environment names production, preprod and submission. Everything the capture did not touch stays a string list and is marked as such in the document.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.fromALiveRun: A dedicated server 1.8.0.13 on this machine, outside the DSH file sandbox - which is what made any of it possible: inside the sandbox every child process fails TLS (Curl error=SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK in the game, schannel: AcquireCredentialsHandle failed in the shell), the environment never resolves, and the log says ENV:[invalid]. Outside it the same binary prints ENV:[production]. The capture used a throwaway self-signed root certificate in the current user's Root store, removed again at the end of every run.
backendApiAndOwnerToken.stillOpen: The capture covers the dedicated server's own traffic only: the game client was deliberately left outside the proxy (with it inside, the client failed to initialise), so the server browser, the join queue a client can be put into, servers/join, the session login and the identity endpoints are unobserved. Storage, groups, notifications, the news feed, the server configs in the cloud, the service-status endpoints and the servers/* family remain a list of strings with no method or URL, and which prefix and host each of those contexts uses is not observed; GET /game-api/api/v1.0/dummy is observed but unexplained beyond its name. The heartbeat's timing is one sample (61 s repeatedly); what the answer's gameEvents array can carry is unknown. What -backendEnv changes was not established (with preprod the hosts were identical, and ENV:[...] is printed only on failures). What the owner loses with a lost token is still unmeasured, and whether server.json's root serverId/ownerType are taken from the token is still unverified.

notes: This file is the only hand-written file in data/ — everything else there is generated by tools/build-data.mjs from docs/en/.
